label: KVP-3600, symptom 'thermal_derate'
headline: Seven afternoon derate tickets on KVP-3600 inverters look like the units' own high-ambient protection working as designed — 6 of 376 units, self-recovering, no outages — so hold at monitoring until Kelvara confirms the derate setpoint against spec.
action: Consolidate the four open Kelvara cases (WO-2025-00688, WO-2025-00908, WO-2026-00571, WO-2026-00586) into a single vendor query for the KVP-3600 published derate curve and firmware thermal setpoint, and track afternoon derate MWh on the six named assets through the next hot season — re-open as a warranty claim only if derate is confirmed below the published ambient envelope or event count grows.
reasoning: H2 (text artifact) does not survive the control set: the controls are templated in exactly the same way — WO-2025-00179 and WO-2026-00286 are near-identical overcurrent narratives, and WO-2025-00770 and WO-2025-00465 are near-identical undervoltage narratives — so verbatim phrasing is a corpus-wide narration habit, not evidence that these seven events are one event double-counted; the members carry six distinct asset IDs across four sites and three summers, so they are distinct physical events. H4 is weakened because one member sits at coastal Tidemarsh Bay (WO-2025-00720), not only at the desert sites. What the members actually describe, however, is textbook designed high-ambient protection: a tightly clustered 10-12% afternoon limit, no stored fault and nothing to reset (WO-2025-00670), and the fullest inspection in the set found filters, intake screens and plenum clear with all six fans turning and cabinet temperature recovering after sundown unaided (WO-2026-00586) — H3's signature. H1 cannot be excluded (KVP36-2419B-0361 recurred in WO-2024-00163 and WO-2025-00688, and fans/filters were consumed in WO-2025-00908 and WO-2026-00571 with no recorded benefit), but nothing here shows derate occurring below the published operating envelope, and the affected serials (2419B, 2420B, 2426B, 2427C, 2428C, 2436C) overlap the same bands as non-derating control units (KVP36-2420B-0350, KVP36-2420B-0355, KVP36-2421B-0201). Impact is small and bounded — partial afternoon curtailment on 6 of 376 units over roughly two years, 28.5 labour hours total, no outages and no hard trips — so this does not warrant commercial action now.
contradicting: Three signals argue for a real model defect rather than designed behaviour: KVP36-2419B-0361 recurred across two separate seasons (WO-2024-00163, WO-2025-00688); parts were consumed with no recorded improvement (cooling fan x3 in WO-2025-00908, air filter set in WO-2026-00571); and every OEM case remains pending (WO-2025-00688, WO-2025-00908, WO-2026-00571, WO-2026-00586) rather than closed as normal operation. A same-model unit also logged unexplained low airflow with clean filters and all fans running (WO-2025-00920), hinting at a cooling-control issue the current data cannot resolve. If Kelvara confirms the derate setpoint activates below the published ambient envelope, this flips to a warranty-grade H1 finding.

population_detail.description: Six distinct KVP-3600 assets observed exhibiting afternoon thermal derate (KVP36-2419B-0361, KVP36-2436C-0275, KVP36-2426B-0289, KVP36-2428C-0169, KVP36-2420B-0352, KVP36-2427C-0381) out of a 376-unit KVP-3600 installed base; fleet-wide exposure would only apply if a common firmware setpoint is confirmed, which this data does not establish.
population_detail.basis: Distinct asset_ids appearing in the seven cluster member work orders, against total_installed for KVP-3600 in installed_base.

hypotheses.statement: KVP-3600 inverters carry a cooling/fan-control or thermal-threshold defect (likely firmware-set derate point, not blocked airflow) that causes an unlogged 10-12% afternoon power limit at high ambient, and it is progressive/recurring on the same units regardless of fan or filter replacement.
predictions: Repeat WOs on the same asset IDs across separate seasons (e.g. KVP36-2419B-0361 appears in 2024-09 and 2025-07); recurrence flag true on a majority of members.

Members where parts were actually consumed ('cooling fan x3', 'air filter set') generate a follow-up thermal_derate WO on the same asset within the next hot season, i.e. no measurable benefit_pct anywhere in the cluster.
Resolution codes stay in the ESCALATED / VENDOR-REFERRED / NO-FAULT-FOUND family with outcome 'pending' or 'no_change'; essentially zero 'REPAIRED' closures.
Affected units share a serial/build band or firmware revision field; unaffected KVP-3600s in the same cohort at equally hot sites cluster in a different band.
Cluster count grows year-over-year (1 in 2024, 3 in 2025, 3 in 2026 by June) faster than cohort growth.
discriminating_evidence: A firmware/serial field that splits the 7 affected units from the ~369 unaffected ones at comparable site temperature separates H1 from H3/H4.
If any unit was fully repaired (fan controller or board swap) and then produced no further thermal_derate WO in the following summer, H1 is supported and H3 (as-designed behaviour) is weakened.
If peer-model inverters at the SAME sites also log afternoon derate WOs on the same dates, H1 loses to H4.

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is largely a text/extraction artifact: several narratives are verbatim or near-verbatim copies of one another and three of seven come from a single technician, so 'thermal_derate' is a labelling convention applied to KVP units rather than a distinct physical event population.
predictions: String-similarity check finds byte-identical or >95% identical narrative bodies across WO-2024-00163 / WO-2025-00720 and across WO-2025-00688 / WO-2025-00908 / WO-2026-00571 / WO-2026-00586.
Author concentration: TECH-0103 authors 3/7 members; the whole cluster is written by <=6 distinct techs out of the site technician population.

Peer models show non-zero counts of a semantically equivalent symptom under a different key (e.g. 'low_output', 'underperformance', 'high_temp'), so the peer_median_rate of 0.0 is a taxonomy artifact rather than a real absence.
Component field is internally inconsistent (one member tagged 'string_inverter', the rest 'central_inverter') for the same model, indicating field-fill noise.
Environment tags split between 'high_ambient_heat' and 'none_mentioned' on narratives describing the same afternoon-heat scenario.
discriminating_evidence: Run exact-duplicate detection on narrative text: if the templated WOs are removed, does n drop below ~4 and the rate become indistinguishable from peers?
Re-map peer-model symptom keys onto a common vocabulary; if peer rate rises to ~0.015-0.02, the lift disappears and H2 explains the candidate without any defect.
Rate of thermal_derate per technician-authored WO: if it is flat across techs, H2 weakens; if it is driven by one or two authors, H2 is favoured.

hypotheses.statement: This is the inverter's designed high-ambient protection operating normally — cabinet temperature rises through the afternoon and recovers after sundown with no stored fault — and the WOs reflect operator unfamiliarity rather than a failure.
predictions: Derate magnitude is tightly clustered (10-12% reported in every narrative) rather than dispersed or worsening, consistent with a fixed spec curve.
Every event self-resolves after sundown with no intervention; no member shows a hard trip, no fault code stored, no parts required to restore output.
Total lost energy is small and bounded: 20.4 MWh over 7 events (~2.9 MWh each), of the order of a few afternoon hours of partial curtailment, not an outage.
All members fall in the hot half of the year (June-September) with none in October-May.
Inspection-only actions ('all six fans turning, filters and plenum clear') find no physical fault in the units that were thoroughly checked.
discriminating_evidence: Compare cabinet-temperature-vs-output on an affected unit against a healthy same-model unit at the same site and hour: if both derate identically, H3 holds and H1 falls.
Check DC:AC ratio / nameplate loading at the affected positions — if derating units are systematically the most heavily loaded, H3 is supported.
If any unit derates at ambient temperatures well below the published operating envelope, H3 is falsified in favour of H1.

hypotheses.statement: Ordinary variation plus discrete summer heat events: 7 events in 376 units (1.9% over ~2 years) is an unremarkable rate, and the apparent model specificity comes from KVP-3600 being concentrated at the hottest sites (Bitter Draw, Ashvale Dry Lake, Joshua Fork) rather than from any model property.
predictions: Member dates concentrate on a small number of calendar days/weeks that coincide with site-wide heat-related WO spikes across all asset classes (tracker, transformer, comms).
Site mix of the KVP-3600 cohort is skewed toward desert/high-ambient sites relative to peer-model cohorts; peer models with zero thermal_derate WOs are installed predominantly at cooler sites.
After stratifying by site (or by site-season), the KVP-3600 thermal_derate rate falls within the range of same-site peer models.
No single asset dominates: excluding the one repeat asset, the remaining events are one-per-unit and spread across 4 sites.
Poisson expectation for 376 units over the observation window makes 7 events unsurprising; comparable clusters of n=5-8 exist for other model-symptom pairs with equally 'null' lift.
discriminating_evidence: Site-stratified rate comparison: if same-site peer models also show ~2% thermal derate, H4 explains everything and H1 is unnecessary.
If the cluster spans many independent hot days across three summers rather than 2-3 discrete heat waves, the 'discrete weather event' part of H4 weakens.
If KVP-3600 units at cool-climate sites also produce thermal_derate WOs, H4 falls and H1 or H3 is favoured.

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
